record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
record.original_question: In bi-connexive logics such as 2C, determine what happens if the strong negation that toggles between refutability and provability is removed, and more generally investigate the resulting systems when one also considers dispensing with primitive verum and falsum constants.

evidence.quote: Open problem 9 What is the effect on connexive logics like 2C if the strong negation, which toggles between refutability and provability, is dispensed with?

Moreover, concerns regarding the constructiveness of a logical system might motivate one to develop a critical attitude towards primitive verum and falsum constants, ⊤ and ⊥, that are present in 2C. Then doing without strong negation, ⊤, and ⊥ is another path to investigate.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work introduces a system B2C obtained from 2C by dropping the toggling strong negation as well as the constants ⊤ and ⊥, and shows it is still a connexive, bi-connexive, negation-inconsistent and non-trivial logic, with mostly undefinability results characterizing the weak language. Related bilateralist proof-theoretic investigations of the negation-free fragment have also appeared. The broader investigation of all such resulting systems is still ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Bi-connexive logic, bilateralism, and negation inconsistency
status_evidence.snippet: B2C is obtained by dropping the toggling negation and the constants ⊤ and ⊥ from 2C; it is shown to be connexive, bi-connexive, negation-inconsistent and non-trivial, despite lacking primitive negation or the constants.
status_evidence.claim: A successor system B2C addressing the open problem has been constructed and studied.

status_evidence.title: Contradictions without negation and a proof-theoretic, bilateralist account of connexive logics (Sara Ayhan)
status_evidence.snippet: Bilateralist proof-theoretic treatment of connexive logics where contradictions are understood without primitive negation.
status_evidence.claim: Active follow-up work investigates the negation-free bilateralist setting motivated by the same problem.
